description.value: The study examined how subjective and objective sleep quality relate to emotion-regulation brain function during an fMRI reappraisal task in patients with anxiety and depressive disorders.

spans.text: Therefore, the primary aim of the current study was to examine the relationship between sleep and reappraise-related neurofunctional activity in anxious and depressed patients with the PSQI and actigraphy.

value: We hypothesized greater sleep disturbance would correspond with less engagement in frontal regions critically involved in reappraisal.
Behaviorally, we hypothesized a lack of concordance between self-report and actigraphy estimates of sleep quality.
